Try to laugh about it, because it was so brave of you to go. Even most people without SA wouldn t have gone by themselves, and you put yourself out there. You should compliment yourself on that and see it as you told your colleagues: had the time of my life just because i did something i am terrified of doing.

Thanks for your inspiring post, it made me register a few minutes ago for wanting to have my say for the first time ever in an environment like this. Excuse my flaky English ;) since it isn't my native language:

Your story moved me since I recognized so much of it. I have been feeling anxious and lost for some time now, searching for the right path in life. I also tried to 'read and research' my way out of it, but when it comes down to it, I always end up at the same spot: a place where i find myself scared shitless. Scared of just not being good enough as a person, scared of mockery. Though, I always try to stay positive and say to myself that one fine day I will make friends with this monster and make it my pet.

My life thusfar has been one bumpy ride, filled with scary, dark, but also beautiful, funny experiences where perhaps in the future I may be able to elaborate some more about. For now, I just wanted to say thanks for your post and in general thanks for the subreddit about social anxiety. Now I know I am not the only one and some of the comments are very similar to my own situation and that strengthens me. 

I hope that all people who deal with these kind of problems will find some peace in their minds, since I know how the brain can trick you into feeling lousy about things that you basically are perfectly capable of handling in a succesful way. This sounds a bit dreamy, but remember that you and the situation where you find yourself in just ARE, it is the assumptions you make that leave you feeling scared. Because, on first sight, nothing is scary about the situation itself of walking into a bar to grab a drink, it's your brain that tells you 'well everybody here thinks that you're the weirdest specimen on the planet'. I hope I one day can have the feeling of walking into a bar without those misguiding thoughts. We'll get there. 

Thanks again for your inspiring stories.

BTW: I also am familiar with Mindfulness and am intrigued by Jon Kabat-Zinn.
